answer: What stops a raft of mirrors from reflecting infinite lanterns at dawn? Each lamp-mirror must cast its beam on a floating jetty, its angle registered at sub-millisecond precision. An attacker spinning fake mirrors burns 0.09 seconds of irreducible, serial beam-timing recompute per head—no bulk mirror farms can pre-latch the jetty’s swaying period, forcing each Sybil to foot the bill in real time.
